methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $30M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Cemvita is a Series B climate & energy company founded by Moji and Tara Karimi that has raised $30M to date. The valuation assessment draws on a competitive universe of 9 private peers and 1 public comparable (Lilium via LNZA), spanning advanced energy infrastructure and materials sectors at Series C and adjacent stages.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression anchoring total capital raised to a 1.9x Series B step-up multiplier yields $57M. Peer-median valuation across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—KoBold Metals ($3.0B), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B), and Amogy ($700M)—produces a median of $1.0B, with a range of $700M to $3.0B. The wide peer dispersion reflects heterogeneity in technology maturity and capital intensity within climate-tech.

The triangulated valuation range is $48M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $528M. The stage-progression method anchors the lower bound; the peer-median method dominates the upper half. Key uncertainties include technology readiness level relative to the peer set, path to near-term unit economics, and regulatory/commodity price exposure specific to Cemvita's application. The $480M spread between low and high reflects meaningful uncertainty around whether Cemvita's risk profile and progress trajectory align more closely with early-stage or later-stage climate-tech benchmarks.
